text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass; to understand the extent of your condition, could you describe when you first noticed these symptoms and if there is any associated pain or weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and nulliparity, along with the rapid onset of respiratory and abdominal symptoms, could you tell me if you have noticed any changes in your menstrual cycles or if the shortness of breath is worse when lying flat?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fatigue is concerning; do you have any history of deep vein thrombosis, recent long travel, or a family history of blood clotting disorders? Also, please report if you have noticed any distended neck veins or sudden chest pain. REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer, REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with malignant ascites and pleural effusion.
The normal D-Dimer effectively rules out a pulmonary embolism as the primary cause of your shortness of breath. The combination of a large ovarian mass, significant ascites, and respiratory symptoms in a 40-year-old woman strongly suggests advanced ovarian carcinoma causing pressure on the diaphragm or a malignant pleural effusion.
